children: Norway's central bank held its key interest rate Thursday, but kept open the possibility of further policy tightening should inflation remain high.

Norges Bank held its key rate at 4.5% as expected by investors, having raised it by a quarter-point in its last meeting in September. Policymakers said "restrictive monetary policy is still needed to bring inflation down to target within a reasonable time horizon."
"Inflation is too high. It will likely be necessary to keep the policy rate elevated for a time, and we are prepared to raise the policy rate if needed," Gov. Ida Wolden Bache said.

The decision to hold the key rate came a week after the European Central Bank also stood pat. Like the ECB, Norges Bank has raised rates twice since the start of the war in the Middle East that led energy prices to surge.
Prior to the announcement, investors had expected rates to remain at their current level until at least the end of next year, according to LSEG data.
